parsed.explanation: The state’s strong, statewide public-accommodation protections, gender-identity hate-crime enhancements, and visitor-relevant care shield are meaningful positives. It has no documented local facilities ban, and its laws provide a substantially more protective local setting than many jurisdictions. But these protections do not override the national regime: passport-marker restrictions and entry guidance create real risks of scrutiny, refusal, or serious immigration consequences, while national restrictions also affect access to some government-funded single-sex facilities and custody. The state’s protection laws are not shown to have reliably remedied visitor-facing discrimination in practice, and enforcement data are limited. The shield law’s scope is also unresolved. I therefore rate this below jurisdictions without active national traveler-facing restrictions, but above the national picture alone because of the state’s comparatively protective laws. The precise outcomes at entry and in facilities remain uncertain; that uncertainty is not evidence of safety.
